outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of the northern and central Great Plains during the late afternoon and evening. The most likely corridor for these to occur is across parts of central and eastern North Dakota.

sections.title: Northern Rockies/Great Plains
sections.text: A shortwave trough over the Pacific Northwest will progress across the northern Rockies with minor mid-level impulses ejecting downstream across the northern to central Great Plains. Primary focus for severe thunderstorm development during the late afternoon will be tied to these minor impulses. A surface front will arc east then north-northeast from the primary cyclone over the Bighorn Basin. The ND portion of the boundary should have the greatest buoyancy as the 12Z Bismarck sounding sampled rich boundary-layer moisture (mean mixing ratios of 14 g/kg) beneath very steep mid-level lapse rates (approaching 9 C/km). MLCAPE within this portion of the front should reach 3000-4000 J/kg. Convergence along the sharpening front is expected to result in convective initiation across parts of central ND in the late afternoon. The strong buoyancy will support intense updrafts, including a few initial supercells capable of large hail. Limited vertical shear with eastward extent will contribute to storm clustering/upscale growth in the evening, with the potential for damaging winds/some hail persisting toward eastern ND/northwest MN. sections.title: Central Great Plains
sections.text: Multiple sub-regional influences should lead to peak severe risk during late afternoon to mid evening in a corridor spanning NE/northeast CO and northern/western KS. Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop off the Front Range and along a High Plains surface trough by mid to late afternoon. These storms are likely to intensify some as they develop generally eastward within a moderate buoyancy/modest deep-layer shear environment. Multiple semi-organized storm clusters should evolve across the region with isolated severe wind gusts expected to be the primary risk.

sections.title: Southeast VA to northeast SC
sections.text: A weak surface front will shift south from VA into NC. Associated convergence amid a moist air mass characterized by low to mid 70s surface dewpoints will aid in scattered thunderstorms. Weak deep-layer shear will limit potential for organization and modest mid-level lapse rates should temper updraft strength somewhat. However, a few locally damaging wind gusts may occur with downbursts amid 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE. ..Grams/Cook.. 07/08/2019

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across portions of the northern and central Great Plains through late evening. Damaging wind gusts and hail will be the main threat, through a tornado or two can not be ruled out, mainly across North Dakota.

sections.title: 20z Update - Northern Plains Vicinity
sections.text: Overall forecast philosophy remains similar to the previous outlook. The Enhanced risk area over ND and MN has been adjusted and re-oriented along currently surface boundary and line of convection stretching from southwest to northeast across ND. The area was also expanded southward along the Red River Valley to include more of southeast ND and adjacent northwest MN. Vigorous convection continues to develop along/just ahead of the surface boundary in an environment of increasing effective shear and MLCAPE greater than 3500 J/km per 19z Mesoanalysis. Individual cells will lift northeast but the line as a whole will shift east/southeast into backed southeasterly low level flow and atop the upper ridge over the Upper Midwest. Damaging wind will be the primary threat into late evening. If any discrete cells develop along or ahead of the line, a very large hail threat also will exist. With backed surface winds and mean mixing ratio values around 14 g/kg a tornado could also accompany a discrete cell, through this threat is rather conditional.

sections.title: Elsewhere
sections.text: The previous outlook is on track and no other changes have been made. ..Leitman.. 07/08/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT Mon Jul 08 2019/

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across portions of the northern and central Great Plains through late evening. Damaging wind gusts and hail will be the main threat, through a tornado or two can not be ruled out, mainly across North Dakota.

sections.title: 01Z Update
sections.text: ....Northern Plains/Northern High Plains... Organized convective line moving across eastern ND at about 45 mph has produced a few 70+ mph wind gusts over the past hour. Downstream air mass is characterized by temperatures in the upper 70s/low 80s, dewpoints in the upper 60s/low 70s, and strong buoyancy. Expectation is for this line to remain strong for the next several hours as it moves through northwest MN. Farther west, another line of storms is moving across southeast MT and northwest WY. A 56 kt gust was recently reported by the Greybull, WY ASOS (KGEY). Downstream air mass here is a little drier and less buoyant but the surging cold pool and resulting discrete propagation will likely still result in strong wind gusts and occasional hail. More information about this area is available in MCD 1417. Squall line currently moving through western NE/far northwest CO will continue to pose a risk for strong wind gusts. Cell interactions between this line and the thunderstorms developing ahead of this line across south-central NE could act to augment/strengthen the line. Isolated hail is also possible with this more multicellular lead development. Additional information for this area is

sections.title: Coastal Carolinas
sections.text: Widely scattered thunderstorms will continue across the region for the next few hours but the threat for severe thunderstorms has diminished enough to remove the Marginal Risk. An isolated damaging wind gust or two remains possible. ..Mosier.. 07/09/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A threat for marginally severe wind gusts and hail will be likely this afternoon across parts of the Carolinas and far southeast Virginia. Weather watch issuance is not expected across the region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis shows a cold front in southern Virginia with a very moist airmass in place south of the front across the Carolinas. Surface dewpoints are generally in the mid 70s F with temperatures in the lower 90s F. In response, a pocket of moderate to strong instability is located across the eastern half of North Carolina into northern South Carolina where the RAP is analyzing MLCAPE values of 2000 to 3000 J/kg. In addition, RAP forecast soundings in eastern North Carolina show an inverted V-profile. This suggests that there could be a potential for isolated marginally severe downbursts. Hail could also accompany the stronger pulse storms. The severe threat should be maximized around peak heating. ..Broyles.. 07/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will be issued soon for portions of the discussion area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convective towers were deepening along a surface boundary draped from west-southwest to east-northeast across central North Dakota. These towers were in a very unstable environment, with low to mid 70s F dewpoints beneath 8-9C mid-level lapse rates resulting in around 4000-5000 J/kg MUCAPE. Shear profiles are relatively weak, but enough flow in the 300-400 mb layer exists for modest organization, with storms likely to evolve into linear segments while forward-propagating northeastward near and ahead of the front. Large (perhaps significant) hail and severe wind gusts are expected as convection matures. Given the evolving threat, a Severe Thunderstorm Watch is expected within the next half hour or so and will be coordinated with affected WFOs.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Convection continues to deepen across western portions of the discussion area and will pose a gradually increasing hail/wind risk with eastward extent.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The combination of surface heating/destabilization and lift associated with a couple of subtle mid-level impulses over southwestern Montana and northeastern Idaho was resulting in gradually increasing convection over the past hour or so near the Big Horns/Absaroka Range and vicinity. This initial convection was in an environment marginally supportive of severe hail/wind risk (1000-1500 J/kg MUCAPE and 30-40 kt deep shear). However, the downstream environment over north-central Wyoming and southeastern Montana is more moist/unstable (2000-2500 J/kg MUCAPE), with steep lapse rates aloft and mid-50s F dewpoints expected support a greater hail/wind risk as storms migrate eastward. Latest CAMs/model guidance suggests that storms will tend to grow upscale with eastward movement, with a mix of clusters and linear segments expected to evolve through the afternoon. This severe risk will likely necessitate a Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance in the next couple hours or so.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat is expected to develop across parts of the central Plains this afternoon. Isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts should be the primary threats. Weather watch issuance may be needed across the region over the next 1 to 2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest surface analysis shows backed southeast flow across much of the central Plains with a very moist airmass in place. Surface dewpoints range from the upper 50s F in far eastern Colorado to the lower 70s F across much of Kansas and Nebraska. This is contributing to moderate to strong instability over much of the central Plains with the RAP estimating MLCAPE values of 2000 to 3000 J/kg range. In addition to the instability, the convection is being supported by a shortwave trough moving across the central High Plains. Although forecast soundings have 0-6 km shear only in the 20 to 25 kt range over much of the central Plains, steep low-level lapse rates should be enough for damaging wind gusts with the stronger multicells. In addition, steep lapse rates at mid-levels may also support large hailstones with the stronger updrafts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues for WW 498.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Ongoing convection continues along a surface boundary located from near DIK northeastward to about 45 N DVL. Storms have quickly become outflow dominant, which isn't a surprise given weak low-level shear. A couple of brief landspouts were also noted earlier in the lifecycle of the convection. A stout mid-level inversion was noted on the 19Z RAOB from BIS, however, and newer updrafts on the southern end of convection may be struggling against that inhibition, limiting the extent of convection in that area. Nevertheless, where convection is sustained, damaging wind gusts and hail are likely given steep lapse rates aloft and very strong surface-based pre-convective buoyancy. More marginally severe storms are also entering northwestern North Dakota outside of WW 498. The 19Z RAOB from GGW indicates steep (7.5 deg C/km) mid-level lapse rates atop a relatively shallow stable layer which is probably non-existent in areas east where mid-80s surface temperatures exist. Isolated severe hail/wind may be observed with this activity, though it is uncertain if spatial extensions of WW 498 are needed ahead of this activity. ..Cook.. 07/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong/severe wind gusts possible this afternoon. A WW is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of thunderstorms have formed in response to strong diurnal heating in the Texas South Plains. Upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints have helped contribute to 2500-3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Deep-layer shear, per regional VWP, is around 25-30 kts. Weak flow aloft under the influence of the subtropical ridge has confined most of the shear in the lowest 3 km. Storms are expected to remain relatively disorganized, but steep low-level lapse rates may allow a few strong to severe wind gusts to occur as updrafts collapse. Should an organized cold pool develop, the risk for strong wind gusts would increase. Without strong forcing aloft, storms will likely weaken/dissipate shortly after local sunset. No WW is anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms capable of severe wind gusts as well as large hail continue within WW 498. Linear storm mode will favor severe wind gusts as the primary threat. A downstream WW or WW extensions will likely be needed in the next 1-2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms in WW 498 have clustered into several linear segments. Given the extreme buoyancy out ahead of this activity -- 3500-4000 J/kg MLCAPE -- storms will continue to propagate eastward and pose a threat for severe wind gusts. Though deep-layer shear is modest (around 30-35 kts) and storm mode has become more linear, steep level lapse rates will support large hail in the stronger cores. Stronger storms have also developed within southern Manitoba, some of which may move into portions of northern Minnesota. A downstream WW or WW extensions will need to be considered within the next 1-2 hours as activity is expected to maintain its intensity into the early evening. ..Wendt.. 07/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms in WW 499 will continue to pose a threat for severe wind gusts and large hail. Storms are expected to grow upscale and pose primarily a severe wind gust threat with time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storm coverage has been increasing within WW 499 as convection has continued to initiate along the Big Horn Range. Effective deep-layer shear of around 40 kts and increasing MLCAPE (1000-1500 J/kg) downstream of this activity will continue to support organized storms capable of large hail and severe wind gusts. Given the coverage of storms, upscale growth is likely to occur with time and the main threat will transition to severe wind gusts. Some MLCIN still exists downstream, though continued modest mid-level height falls with the approach of the shortwave trough will help to erode remaining inhibition. ..Wendt.. 07/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat should spread across central into eastern portions of ww500 over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early-evening water-vapor imagery suggests a few weak disturbances embedded within southwesterly flow across the southern Rockies/central High Plains region. Lead short wave appears to be influencing multiple thunderstorm clusters over south-central NE. This activity should gradually expand in areal coverage shortly after sunset as LLJ begins to increase across the Plains. Upstream, a secondary short wave is ejecting across central CO and the leading edge of large-scale forcing for ascent appears to be partly responsible for a band of storms that currently stretches from the NE Panhandle, arcing into northeast CO. This activity is fairly well organized and surging east at roughly 25-30kt. Isolated severe wind gusts may accompany this squall line as it spreads across the eastern half of ww500. ..Darrow.. 07/08/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong bowing segment will continue to move east through remainder of WW 498 in northwestern Minnesota. Convection in southern/southeastern North Dakota will continue to pose some risk of severe wind gusts for perhaps another hour or two.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong bowing segment with history of 50-60 mph wind gusts, and a few gusts greater than 70 mph, will continue into portions of western Minnesota. Though buoyancy decreases to the east, a mature cold pool will continue to drive continue updraft initiation for likely for a few more hours. Farther to the south and west, large buoyancy still remains in southeast North Dakota and northeast South Dakota -- around 3000 J/kg MLCAPE per 00Z ABR sounding. With WW 498 set to expire at 9 PM CDT, the question will be whether convection can push southeastward into northeastern South Dakota. Current visible satellite shows wave clouds likely associated with an atmospheric bore. This would indicate at least some MLCIN remaining. KMVX VWP would suggest that the cold pool depth is in the 1000-1500 m range with a more shallow cold pool expected farther south/west where convection has been less robust. Given these observational trends, the current expectation is that convection will struggle to reach LFC and to propagate into northern/northeastern South Dakota. While these trends would make a new WW to the south of WW 498 unlikely, trends will continue to be monitored. ..Wendt.. 07/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe wind gusts and large hail remain possible in WW 499. Trends will be monitored for possible local extensions or a new WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection in southeast Montana and northeast Wyoming has grown upscale into a QLCS. The last few hours of regional radar mosaic imagery indicates that an MCV has developed and is now near Sheridan County, WY. The cluster of storms associated with this feature will likely pose the greatest risk for severe wind gusts in the short term. Other more isolated convection has developed along the surface boundary in the ND/SD/MT border vicinity which will pose the greatest large hail risk. Some uncertainty exists with how far northeast this activity will pose a severe risk, especially as low-level lapse rates weaken. With continued mid-level height falls and the influence of the MCV, it seems probable that some activity will last near or beyond the WW expiration of 9 PM MDT. Trends will need to be monitored for possible local extensions or a new WW. ..Wendt.. 07/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong storms will spread southeast across ww501 over the next few hours. Gusty winds are the primary threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Expanding cold pool across eastern ND/northwest MN should contribute to southeast movement of upper Red River Valley squall line. This cluster of storms has matured into a healthy MCS that should persist into the early-morning hours as it sags southeast across ww501. Veered LLJ should aid this movement and gusty winds are the primary threat. ..Darrow.. 07/09/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
